finding.statement: John Gurney was living at Weymouth, Massachusetts, by 30 May / 2 June 1641 — his earliest firm New England presence.

incoming.explanation: Analysis weighs the printed court order's 'John Porter.'
The service negative keeps the 1641 powder fine from being over-read as evidence of military service (cross-topic).
The 1641 gunpowder-fine remission is the earliest secure record anchoring the footprint's opening (cross-topic: arrival-chronology).

Anderson's GMD assessment cites the 1641 Massachusetts General Court gunpowder-fine order (MBCR 1:331) among its six documentary bases for John — the cited-record relationship behind the published arrival/settlement statement.
The reception reading rests on the 1641 gunpowder-fines record that first places John among named Weymouth men.

sources.excerpt: fined 'for want of gunpowder'; remitted by the General Court, 2 June 1641

finding.statement: The Massachusetts General Court order of 2 June 1641 remitted the fine of John Porter, James Ludden, and John Gurney, incurred "for want of gunpowder."
